sentence_stem: Having been informed of the delay,
correct_completion: the passengers returned to the waiting room.
full_sentence: Having been informed of the delay, the passengers returned to the waiting room.
acceptable_variants: they returned to the waiting room.
the passengers went back to the waiting room.

options.text: the passengers returning to the waiting room.
options.why_wrong: This creates a fragment with no finite main verb, so the sentence is incomplete as a main clause.

options.text: the passengers were returning to the waiting room yesterday.
options.why_wrong: 'Yesterday' conflicts with the perfect participle, which describes an action completed just before the main action.

options.text: the passengers returned to the waiting room.
to return to the waiting room.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive cannot serve as the main verb of the sentence, so the passengers' action is not expressed.

explanation: The perfect passive participle 'Having been informed' expresses an action completed before the main verb. English then requires a finished main clause with a finite verb after the comma. Speakers may be tempted to use a gerund or a progressive form here, but the main verb must be in the simple past to show the sequence of events.
translation: Habiendo sido informados del retraso, los pasajeros regresaron a la sala de espera.
